paragraphs.title: Declaration of Faith and the Covenant Promise

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever.”
easy.q: What will the psalmist sing of for ever?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I have made a covenant with my chosen... I have sworn unto David my servant.”
easy.q: With whom did the LORD make a covenant?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 promises, “Thy seed will I establish for ever, and build up thy throne to all generations.”
easy.q: What did the LORD promise to establish?

medium.explanation: Mercy is built up for ever, and faithfulness is established in the heavens.
medium.q: How are mercy and faithfulness presented in these verses?

medium.explanation: The image of building presents mercy as something lasting and firmly established.
medium.q: What does “Mercy shall be built up for ever” suggest?

medium.explanation: The passage moves from praise of God’s mercy and faithfulness to the covenant with David.
medium.q: What is the main movement of verses 1–5?

answers: The continuing witness of God’s faithfulness
A promise lasting only one day
A message meant only for David
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that God’s faithfulness is to be declared throughout succeeding generations.
Both expressions point to an enduring promise and testimony.
challenge.q: Which pair of expressions most strongly emphasizes permanence?

answers: The establishment of David’s seed and throne
challenge.explanation: The covenant centers on David’s offspring and the lasting establishment of his throne.
challenge.q: What is the focus of the covenant promise?

paragraphs.title: God’s Greatness and Rule over Creation

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “And the heavens shall praise thy wonders, O LORD.”
easy.q: Who praises the wonders of the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “Thou rulest the raging of the sea.”
Verse 14 says, “Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne.”
easy.q: What are the habitation of God’s throne?

medium.explanation: The LORD stills the waves and rules the raging sea, showing His supreme power.
medium.q: What does God’s rule over the raging sea demonstrate?

answers: To be treated with awe and respect
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the reverence due to God among those around Him.
medium.q: What does “to be had in reverence” mean?

answers: They characterize God’s rule and presence
medium.explanation: Justice and judgment establish His throne, while mercy and truth go before His face.
medium.q: How do justice, judgment, mercy, and truth function in the passage?

answers: God’s rule over high places only
The separation of creation from God
challenge.explanation: The passage presents God as Lord over heaven, earth, the sea, and the nations.
challenge.q: What does the passage’s movement from heaven to earth and sea emphasize?

answers: To show the breadth of created space rejoicing in God’s name
challenge.explanation: These regions and mountains represent the created world rejoicing in God’s name.
challenge.q: Why are the north, the south, Tabor, and Hermon mentioned together?

answers: They succeed because of their enemies
Their protection is unrelated to God
God is their defence, and His favor exalts their horn
challenge.explanation: The LORD is their defence, and in His favor their horn is exalted.
challenge.q: How are the people connected with God’s protection and favor?

easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “I have found David my servant.”
The verse says, “with my holy oil have I anointed him.”

answers: His father, God, and rock of salvation
easy.explanation: David would say, “Thou art my father, my God, and the rock of my salvation.”
easy.q: What would David call the LORD?

answers: Strengthen him and defeat his foes
medium.explanation: God promises that His hand and arm will strengthen David and that his foes will be beaten down.
medium.q: What did the LORD promise to do for David against his enemies?

answers: His strength and standing will be raised
medium.explanation: In this royal context, an exalted horn represents increased power and honor.
medium.q: What does “his horn shall be exalted” signify?

answers: To express his elevated status among kings
medium.explanation: The next phrase explains the title: David will be “higher than the kings of the earth.”

answers: The anointing is followed by God’s promise to establish and strengthen him
The anointing removes his royal calling
The anointing concerns only human weakness
challenge.explanation: After describing David’s anointing, the LORD promises that His hand and arm will strengthen him.
challenge.q: How are David’s anointing and strengthening related?

answers: That David will become a fisherman
That he will refuse to reign
challenge.explanation: Within the royal context, the sea and rivers represent the reach of David’s power.
challenge.q: What does setting David’s hand in the sea and his right hand in the rivers symbolize?

answers: The seed is unrelated to David
God’s mercy and covenant continue with David and his seed
challenge.explanation: The passage promises lasting mercy to David and endurance for his seed and throne.
challenge.q: How are David and his seed connected in the covenant promise?

paragraphs.title: The Conditions and Permanence of the Covenant

easy.explanation: Verse 30 says, “If his children forsake my law.”
Verse 32 says, “Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with stripes.”
easy.q: How would their iniquity be visited?

answers: Break His covenant or fail in faithfulness
easy.explanation: God says, “My covenant will I not break,” and will not allow His faithfulness to fail.
easy.q: What did the LORD promise not to do?

answers: Sin brings discipline, but does not remove God’s mercy
medium.explanation: The children may be chastened, but God will not utterly take away His lovingkindness.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the children’s sin and the covenant?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the promise God has spoken and sworn to keep.
medium.q: What does “the thing that is gone out of my lips” refer to?

answers: A throne enduring as the sun and moon
medium.explanation: The throne is compared with the enduring sun and moon, emphasizing lasting stability.
medium.q: Which image most strongly conveys permanence?

answers: People have no responsibility for their actions
The covenant depends only on military power
challenge.explanation: The passage combines judgment for disobedience with God’s continuing mercy and faithfulness.
challenge.q: What moral balance is presented in these verses?

answers: It emphasizes the certainty of the promise
It describes the fall of the strongholds
challenge.explanation: God’s oath assures David that His covenant promise will not be false or withdrawn.
challenge.q: Why is the oath that God will not lie unto David important?

challenge.explanation: Their regular and enduring presence illustrates the promised permanence of David’s throne.
challenge.q: What do the sun and moon symbolize in relation to the throne?

paragraphs.title: The Poet’s Lament over David’s Fallen House

easy.explanation: Verse 38 says, “But thou hast cast off and abhorred.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say the LORD has done?

answers: They were broken down and brought to ruin
They were moved into the sea
easy.explanation: The LORD is accused of breaking down the hedges and bringing the strongholds to ruin.
The passage describes spoil, reproach, rejoicing enemies, and failure in battle.
easy.q: What characterized the end of the royal period described here?

answers: An eternal royal promise versus humiliation and collapse
medium.explanation: The earlier verses promise endurance, while this section describes the apparent ruin of David’s house.
medium.q: What is the main contrast between this section and the earlier promises?

answers: Destroyed or reduced them to desolation
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the destruction of the kingdom’s defenses.
medium.q: What does “brought his strong holds to ruin” mean?

answers: A stronger army and a larger throne
Broken defenses, plunder, and defeat in battle
medium.explanation: The verses move from ruined defenses to plunder, enemy rejoicing, and military defeat.
medium.q: What sequence led to the shame of David’s house?

answers: The king’s military strength has been weakened
The king has conquered every enemy
The sword has become a sign of peace
challenge.explanation: The image of the sword’s edge being turned indicates defeat and ineffective warfare.
challenge.q: What does turning the edge of the sword suggest?

challenge.explanation: The LORD is said to make all David’s enemies rejoice, and David becomes a reproach to his neighbors.
challenge.q: How do the enemies respond to David’s fall?

answers: The throne was exalted to heaven
challenge.explanation: Casting the throne to the ground pictures the downfall and humiliation of the monarchy.
challenge.q: What does casting the throne down to the ground signify?

paragraphs.title: A Plea amid Human Mortality and the Covenant Crisis

easy.explanation: He asks, “How long, LORD? wilt thou hide thyself for ever?”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask about God’s hiddenness?

answers: It is brief, and death is certain
easy.explanation: He asks who can live without seeing death and remembers how short his time is.
easy.q: What does the psalmist remember about human life?

easy.explanation: The final verse says, “Blessed be the LORD for evermore. Amen, and Amen.”

answers: To recall the covenant sworn to David
medium.explanation: He asks the LORD to remember the lovingkindnesses sworn unto David in truth.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist appeal to God’s former lovingkindnesses?

medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that human life is brief and cannot be prolonged indefinitely.
medium.q: What does “my time is short” emphasize?

answers: Only the strength of the enemies
The reproach borne by God’s servants
medium.explanation: He asks the LORD to remember the reproach of His servants and the reproach against His anointed.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to remember?

answers: It shows there is little time to wait for deliverance
It removes the need for the covenant
It proves that people are immortal
challenge.explanation: The shortness of life makes the request for God’s intervention urgent.
challenge.q: How does human mortality intensify the plea?

answers: Reproach against God’s servants and anointed also dishonors God’s name
challenge.explanation: The psalmist presents the enemies’ reproach against God’s servants and anointed as a matter requiring God’s attention.
challenge.q: How are the reproach of the servants and the reproach of the anointed related?

answers: It closes the lament with believing affirmation
challenge.explanation: Despite the crisis and lament, the psalm ends by blessing the LORD with a faithful affirmation.
challenge.q: How does “Amen, and Amen” function at the end of the psalm?
